text:
On the morning of 14 March 2031, the wind off the estuary carried the smell of diesel and salt across the old Port Ansgar quays, where cranes have stood idle for the better part of a generation. It was here, in a city long accustomed to being passed through rather than chosen, that Kestrelline Rail announced it would build its new maintenance depot.

Maren Tolliver, the company's Chief Infrastructure Officer, confirmed the Port Ansgar location, which appears in the Fleet Maintenance Expansion Plan released at Kestrelline's spring investor briefing.

The depot is budgeted at 412 million credits and will employ 1,150 staff once operational. For a port that once measured its fortunes in tonnage, the figure invites a quieter kind of reckoning: what it means to be built upon again, and what the city will ask of the railway in return.
